name: Krause Music Store
key_features: Sullivan's last building, with plant-like curving forms framing the picture window.

name: George H. Fallon Federal Office Building
key_features: 17-storey International Style tower clad in Minnesota granite, part of Charles Center.

name: Strom Thurmond Federal Building and U.S. Courthouse
key_features: Monolithic office tower paired with a long, low courthouse; recessed windows with protruding hoods.

name: Haydarpaşa Terminal
key_features: Neo-classical station on land reclaimed from the sea, resting on 1,100 wooden piles.

name: Hagia Sophia
by: Isidore of Miletus, Anthemius of Tralles
key_features: One of the first buildings with a fully pendentive dome, about 33 m across after rebuilding.

name: Istanbul Lütfi Kırdar Convention and Exhibition Center
by: Paolo Vietti-Violi, Şinasi Şahingiray, Fazıl Aysu
key_features: Opened 1949 as the country's only indoor sports and exhibition hall; extended underground in 2009.

name: Milad Tower
key_features: Octagonal base tied to traditional Iranian architecture; steel head of 12 floors with a revolving restaurant.

name: Tomb of Ferdowsi
key_features: Achaemenid-style tomb: a cubical upper structure with four pillars around it, on a wide base.

name: Tomb of Saadi
key_features: Eight brown stone pillars at the front; octagonal interior with marble walls and a blue arch.

name: Sursock Museum
by: Jean-Michel Wilmotte and Jacques Abou Khaled (extension)
key_features: 1912 villa expanded with four new underground floors beneath the garden; reopened 8 October 2015.

name: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque
key_features: Five domes, all of light blue tiles; inaugurated in 2008.

name: Jewish National Institutions House
key_features: Administrative complex whose windows recall the slits in the Old City walls; second storey finished 1936.

name: Jerusalem Great Synagogue
key_features: Sanctuary seats 850 men and 550 women; inaugurated on Tu B'Av 1982.

name: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) campus
key_features: HOK master plan with wind towers and solar panels; world's largest LEED Platinum campus.

name: Riyadh TV Tower
key_features: 170 m television tower, Saudi Arabia's tallest structure until 2000.

name: Yerevan Opera Theatre
key_features: Opened 1933; hall finished 1939 under Tamanian's son; large-scale works ended 1953.

name: Government House, Baku
key_features: Built 1936-1952 to a design by Lev Rudnev and V. Munts; designed for 5,500 people.

name: National Library of Armenia
key_features: Main building follows Tamanian's project; the 'Tamanyan style' reinterprets medieval Armenian architecture.

name: Parliament of Georgia (Rustaveli Avenue)
key_features: Reinforced concrete clad in tufa and granite, with a monumental arcade and arch pediment.

name: Ismailiyya Palace
key_features: Venetian Gothic palace built 1908-1913 for Musa Naghiyev.

name: Martinelli Building
key_features: Brazil's first skyscraper; largest concrete-framed building in the world when it opened.

name: Mineirão
by: Eduardo Mendes Guimarães Júnior, Caspar Garreto
key_features: Pseudo-elliptical concrete superstructure, tested first as a scale 'mini-Mineirão' section.

name: Maracanã Stadium
by: Waldir Ramos, Raphael Galvão, Miguel Feldman, Oscar Valdetaro, Pedro Paulo B. Bastos, Orlando Azevedo, Antônio Dias Carneiro
key_features: Opened in 1950 and then the world's largest stadium; construction was only finished in 1965.

name: Teatro Amazonas
key_features: Opera house whose dome is covered in 36,000 ceramic tiles in Brazil's national colours.

name: Teatro Vila Velha
key_features: Modern-style theatre contrasting with the neoclassical buildings of the nearby Passeio Público.

name: Municipal Market of São Paulo
by: Francisco Ramos de Azevedo, Felisberto Ranzini
key_features: Market hall with 72 stained-glass pieces in 32 panels showing local food production; inaugurated 1933.

name: Matarazzo Building (São Paulo City Hall)
key_features: Italian rationalist design resembling Art Deco; now São Paulo's city hall.

name: Palace of Justice of São Paulo
by: Francisco Ramos de Azevedo, Ricardo Severo, Arnaldo Villares
key_features: One of Brazil's first buildings with a metal structure, mixing baroque and neoclassical elements.

name: Ulysses Guimarães Convention Center
key_features: Built 1973-1979; its north wing holds a Master Auditorium for more than 3,000 people.

name: Pacaembu Stadium
by: Escritório Técnico Ramos de Azevedo - Severo e Villares
key_features: Art Deco stadium built 1938-1940 and listed by CONDEPHAAT in 1998.

name: Theatro Municipal do Rio de Janeiro
key_features: Eclectic Paris Opera-inspired design; outer walls carry names of classic European and Brazilian artists.

name: Theatro da Paz
key_features: Neoclassical theatre with columned patios on each side and horseshoe-shaped seating.

name: Estação da Luz
key_features: Prefabricated structure made in Scotland, assembled in Glasgow, then re-erected in São Paulo.

name: São Bento Monastery
by: Francisco Frias de Mesquita, José Fernandes Pinto Alpoim
key_features: Mannerist church with gold-leaf interior; primary example of Portuguese colonial architecture.

name: National Flag Memorial
key_features: Memorial on the Paraná riverbank, main site of Argentina's Flag Day.

name: Usina del Arte
key_features: Former power plant in La Boca reopened in 2012 as a cultural centre.

name: Palacio Legislativo
key_features: Seat of Uruguay's parliament, inaugurated 1925 and a National Historic Monument.

name: Retiro Bus Station
by: Fernando Serra, Jorge Valera, Raúl Petrucci
key_features: Bus terminal nearly 400 m long with 75 gates.

name: Torre Espacial
by: Peter Totter, Wilhelm Dietrich, Peter Wader
key_features: Telecommunications tower with observation decks at 120, 124 and 176 m.

name: Palacio de Justicia (Palacio de Tribunales)
key_features: Law courts on Plaza Lavalle, a National Historic Monument since 1999.

name: Hotel Carrasco
key_features: Seafront hotel and casino inaugurated in 1921, where Einstein stayed in 1925.

name: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos
key_features: Santiago museum for victims of abuses under Pinochet's 1973-1990 government, opened 2010.

name: Teatro del Lago
key_features: Theatre and concert hall on the shore of Lake Llanquihue with a 1,178-seat main hall, opened 2010.

name: Estación Mapocho
key_features: Railway station opened 1913, refitted as a cultural center since 1994.

name: Teatro Municipal de Santiago
by: Claudio Brunet des Baines, Lucien Hénault
key_features: Santiago's main opera house, inaugurated 1857 and rebuilt after an 1870 fire, completed 1873.

name: Palacio de La Moneda
key_features: Seat of the president of Chile, completed 1805 to designs by Joaquín Toesca.

name: Rafael Uribe Uribe Palace of Culture
key_features: Gothic Revival public building in Medellín, built 1925-1937, now a national monument.

name: San Javier Library Park
key_features: One of Medellín's ten library parks, in the San Javier area; opened December 2006.

name: León de Greiff Library Park
key_features: Library park by Giancarlo Mazzanti in Medellín, opened February 2007.

name: National Capitol of Colombia
key_features: Neoclassical seat of Colombian government on Bogotá's Plaza de Bolívar, completed 1926.

name: National Library of Venezuela
key_features: Brutalist national library in Caracas, designed 1981-1989.

name: Torre de David (Centro Financiero Confinanzas)
key_features: Unfinished Caracas tower, construction halted in 1994.

name: Palacio Federal Legislativo
by: Luciano Urdaneta Vargas and Juan Hurtado Manrique
key_features: Venezuelan legislature in Caracas' historic centre, completed 1877.

name: Supreme Court of India
key_features: Plan meant to resemble the scales of justice; central wing under a 27.6 m dome with a colonnaded verandah.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium
by: Gerkan, Marg and Partners (2010 redesign); roof by Schlaich Bergermann Partner
key_features: 53,800 m2 PTFE-membrane roof carried on about 8,500 tonnes of steel; original stadium 1982.

name: Virasat-e-Khalsa
key_features: Honey-coloured stone and steel-clad double-curved roofs around an artificial lake; turrets grouped in fives.

name: Raj Mandir Cinema
key_features: Art Moderne cinema with a meringue-shaped auditorium and nine stars for the Navaratna gems.

name: Humayun's Tomb
by: Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and Sayyid Muhammad
key_features: Double dome on a high drum; red sandstone with white marble, the first such combination at this scale in India.

name: ISKCON Temple (Glory of India)
key_features: One of the largest temple complexes in India, with a 375-seat auditorium and a Vedic cultural centre.

name: St. Peter and St. Paul's Church, Parumala
key_features: Circular plan, 39 m inner diameter, split into three segments by two 16 m chords; seats over 2,000.

name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Telangana State Secretariat
by: Ponni Concessao and Oscar Concessao (OCI Architects)
key_features: Domed Indo-Saracenic-style secretariat, 265 ft tall, with 635 rooms on a 27.9-acre site.

name: Jehangir Art Gallery
key_features: One of the city's early concrete buildings, with a large wavy cantilevered entrance canopy; four exhibition halls.

name: Nehru Centre
key_features: Cylindrical tower on a sloped, landscaped base; 1,000-seat auditorium, planetarium, exhibition galleries.

name: Gateway of India
key_features: 26 m yellow basalt and reinforced-concrete arch, Indo-Saracenic, drawing on 16th-century Gujarati architecture.

name: Ravindra Bharathi
key_features: Auditorium of about 1,000 seats built for Tagore's birth centenary; opened 1961 and renovated in 2005.

name: Mahindra United World College of India
key_features: Hilltop campus of 'wadas' (student house clusters around courtyards) in local materials, near Mulshi Dam.

name: Ranga Shankara
key_features: 320-seat theatre in J.P. Nagar built for about 3 crore, raised mainly through public contributions.

name: Nelum Pokuna Mahinda Rajapaksa Theatre
key_features: Performing-arts theatre inspired by the 12th-century Nelum Pokuna lotus pond at Polonnaruwa.

name: Martyred Intellectuals Memorial
by: Farid Uddin Ahmed and Md Jami-al-Shafi
key_features: Long curved brick wall about 17.7 m tall, broken at the ends to show grief, recalling the Rayer Bazar brickfield.

name: Mausoleum of Three Leaders
by: Masud Ahmad and S. A. Zahiruddin
key_features: Shell-like roof of a hyperbolic paraboloid structure raised over the three graves.

name: Sixty Dome Mosque
key_features: Brick mosque with thick tapered walls in Tughlaq style and a hut-shaped roof; built 1442-1459.

name: Hatirjheel
key_features: Lake and waterfront public space in central Dhaka, opened in 2013; design team led by Iqbal Habib.

name: Islamic Summit Minar
key_features: 47 m marble and stone obelisk beside a reflecting pool, with an underground museum, for the 1974 Islamic Summit.

name: Lahore Expo Centre
by: NESPAK with Nayyar Ali Dada & Associates
key_features: Convention centre in Johar Town with exhibition halls and a convention hall holding two auditoriums.

name: Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry Building
key_features: Anglo-Mughal revival in sandstone with domes, faux minarets and a large arch at the front.

name: Mohatta Palace
key_features: Indo-Saracenic palace in pink Jodhpur and yellow Gizri stone, with nine domes and carved peacock and floral motifs.

name: Frere Hall
key_features: Venetian-Gothic hall in yellow limestone with pointed arches, ribbed vaults, quatrefoils and flying buttresses.

name: Lahore Museum
by: Bhai Ram Singh and John Lockwood Kipling
key_features: Indo-Saracenic red-brick museum housing Gandharan and Indus Valley collections, plus Sadequain's ceiling mural.

name: Nyayo House
by: Ngotho Architects, Ministry of Public Works
key_features: 84 m government tower of 27 floors at Uhuru Highway and Kenyatta Avenue; built 1979-1983.

name: Tintenpalast (Parliament Building)
key_features: Neoclassical parliament building of regional materials, built 1912-1913 by Sander & Kock.

name: Maputo City Hall (Conselho Municipal)
key_features: Neoclassical town hall with a 65 m facade on Independence Square; 1938 competition, built 1941-1947.

name: Maputo Cathedral
by: Marcial Simões de Freitas e Costa
key_features: 61 m concrete and cement cathedral on Independence Square, designed pro bono by a railway engineer; completed 1944.

name: St. George's Cathedral
key_features: Octagonal cathedral by an Italian engineer, called a European reading of Ethiopian church design in a 1938 guide.

name: Munyonyo Martyrs' Shrine
key_features: Church shrine seating 1,600, up to 47 m high, completed 2016 and consecrated 28 October 2017.

name: Hôtel du Lac
key_features: Ten-storey brutalist block of exposed concrete; inverted-pyramid form with cantilevered end stairs.

name: Mausoleum of Aga Khan III
key_features: Central dome on an octagonal drum with arched windows, four corner domes and crenellated parapet walls.

name: FNB Stadium (Soccer City)
key_features: Shaped like a calabash, an African pot; mosaic cladding in fire and earth tones; structure by Schlaich Bergermann.

name: Nelson Mandela Bay Stadium
by: Architectural Design Associates, Dominic Bonnesse Architects
key_features: Roof of white PTFE membrane 'petals' like a flower, nicknamed The Protea; 46,000 permanent seats.

name: Pretoria Railway Station
key_features: Baker's first public building, replacing an 1892 station; roof restored after a 2001 fire.

name: Japan Ukiyo-e Museum
key_features: Private museum holding over 100,000 woodblock prints, the largest collection of its kind.

name: Iwasaki Art Museum
key_features: Art museum set in the gardens of a resort hotel, with works by Kuroda Seiki and Fujishima Takeji.

name: Miyagi Museum of Art
key_features: Collection centres on Miyagi and Tohoku artists, with works by Kandinsky and Klee.

name: National Showa Memorial Museum
key_features: Museum of everyday life during and after World War II, opened in 1999.

name: Memorial Cathedral for World Peace
key_features: Hiroshima cathedral of 1954, listed among Togo Murano's works.

name: Hashima City Hall (1959)
key_features: Town hall of 1959 by Junzo Sakakura; the building was demolished in 2022.

name: Okayama Prefectural Government Office Main Building
key_features: Prefectural government office beside Okayama Castle, listed among Kunio Maekawa's works of 1955.

name: Nima Sand Museum
key_features: Sand museum in Nima, Oda, listed among Shin Takamatsu's works of 1990.

name: Iida City Museum
key_features: Museum of the area's natural history, history and art, opened in 1989.

name: Miyagi Prefectural Library
key_features: Prefectural library in Sendai, listed among Hiroshi Hara's works of 1998.

name: Okayama Symphony Hall
key_features: Concert hall of 2,001 seats, with acoustic design by Nagata Acoustics.
